report.summary: An incident occurred resulting in intermittent database connection errors in payment confirmations due to a configuration change that reduced the maximum database connection pool size on ledger-service from 50 to 5. This triggered connection pool exhaustion, elevated latency, and increased error rates across ledger-service and payments-api starting at 2026-10-06T13:14:00+00:00.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Configuration Change Reducing Database Connection Pool Size Exhausts Ledger Service Connections

supporting.note: Config change on ledger-service at 13:12 reduced db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5, immediately preceding the onset.
Ledger-service latency anomaly began at 13:14, right after the config change.
Ledger-service error rate spiked starting at 13:15.
Payments-api error rate spiked starting at 13:15 as calls to ledger-service failed.
Ledger-service logs show HikariPool connection timeouts indicating pool exhaustion (total=5, active=5) starting at 13:15.
Payments-api logs show errors calling ledger-service due to inability to acquire connections starting at 13:15.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Upstream Traffic Surge Overwhelming Ledger Service

supporting.note: Payments-api error rates spiked during the incident.

contradicting.note: Payments-api RPS shows no abnormal surge or traffic spike during the window.
The config change at 13:12 provides a direct and sufficient explanation for connection exhaustion without needing a traffic spike.

facts.text: Payments-api error rate spiked up starting at 2026-10-06T13:15:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 8.26% at 13:47.
Ledger-service error rate spiked starting at 2026-10-06T13:15:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 10.25% at 13:45.
Ledger-service p99 latency anomaly began at 2026-10-06T13:14:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 7278.17ms.
Ledger-service logs show HikariPool connection timeouts indicating pool exhaustion (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting) starting at 2026-10-06T13:15:05+00:00.
Payments-api logs show errors calling ledger-service due to inability to acquire connections starting at 2026-10-06T13:15:02+00:00.
Ledger-db active connections and cpu percentage dropped significantly starting at 2026-10-06T13:13:00+00:00.
Ledger-service underwent a config change on 2026-10-06 at 13:12 normalizing db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5.

assumptions: The configuration change applied successfully across all running instances of ledger-service instantly.

timeline.event: Config-sync normalizes db.pool.max_size from 50 to 5 on ledger-service
Ledger-db active connections and cpu percentage drop significantly
Ledger-service and payments-api error rates spike
Payments-api logs errors calling ledger-service due to inability to acquire connections
Ledger-service logs HikariPool connection timeouts indicating pool exhaustion

recommended_actions.action: Revert the database connection pool configuration change on ledger-service back to 50
recommended_actions.rationale: Configuration change chg-8919 reduced max pool size to 5, which directly caused database connection pool exhaustion and subsequent errors across dependent services.

recommended_actions.action: Implement validation checks in the config-sync tool to prevent excessively low database connection pool sizes relative to service concurrency and traffic load
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents automated or manual normalization changes from blindly overriding required service resource bounds.

recommended_actions.action: Establish comprehensive automated alerting for sudden drops in database active connections and abnormal database pool wait times
recommended_actions.rationale: Ensures early detection of connection pool constraints before customer-facing request failures cascade.
